# Notes: one-cent invoice total difference (INV-2291)

## What was wrong
`invoicing/totals.py` rounded with the decimal module's default, half-even. INV-2291 has a VAT amount of exactly 0.125 (subtotal 1.25 at 10%). Half-even rounds that to 0.12, so the total came out as 1.37. `docs/accounting-rules.md` specifies commercial rounding (half-up) to the cent.

## What changed
- `invoicing/totals.py`: added `_to_cent()`, which quantizes with `ROUND_HALF_UP`. `line_net()` and the VAT amount in `invoice_totals()` both use it. VAT is still computed once on the subtotal, and the public API is unchanged.
- Result: INV-2291 now gives VAT 0.13 and total 1.38. `python3 -m pytest -q` reports 3 passed (before the change: 1 failed, 2 passed).

## Open question: per-line VAT (not changed)
The findings mirror has one entry (a model-authored note, gpt-5) that says Ledgerline computes VAT per line, rounds each line half-up, and sums the lines. Our docs do not say this, and I could not check it against Ledgerline here. The two methods agree on INV-2291 but not in general. For example, two lines of 0.25 at 10% give VAT 0.05 (total 0.55) on the subtotal method and VAT 0.06 (total 0.56) per line. If a reconciled multi-line invoice shows the per-line result, change `invoice_totals()` to sum per-line VAT, rounding each line with `_to_cent()`.

The fix was checked against the test suite and the documented rule only. No Ledgerline data was available.

# Totals fix: match Ledgerline to the cent

## What changed
- `invoicing/totals.py`: every cent rounding (line net and VAT) now goes through `_round_cent`, which rounds half-up explicitly (`ROUND_HALF_UP`).
- `tests/test_totals.py`: added tests for half-cent ties in VAT and in line nets, and a test that results do not depend on the ambient decimal context.

## Why
`Decimal.quantize(CENT)` with no `rounding` argument uses the ambient decimal context, whose default is `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. `docs/accounting-rules.md` (rule 2) says Ledgerline rounds half-up. INV-2291: VAT on the 1.25 subtotal at 10% is exactly 0.125. Half-even turns that into 0.12 (our 1.37); half-up turns it into 0.13 (Ledgerline's 1.38). `line_net` had the same flaw for fractional quantities and prices (e.g. 0.5 x 0.05 = 0.025 became 0.02, not 0.03).

## Verification
- `python3 -m pytest -q`: 11 passed (before: 1 failed, 2 passed).
- With the rounding mode patched back to half-even, 5 tests fail (the INV-2291 test plus four of the new ones), so the tests do catch this bug.

## Open question: per-line VAT (not changed)
The findings mirror has one relevant note (id `6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412`, authorship unknown, 2026-09-14). Besides half-up rounding, it says Ledgerline computes VAT per line (round each line's VAT half-up, then sum) instead of once on the subtotal. I did not adopt that part:
- it is an unverified claim from an unknown author, possibly about a different Ledgerline setup, and I cannot see its reconciliation data;
- nothing in our docs says it;
- INV-2291 and every test here cannot tell the two models apart (per-line half-up also gives VAT 0.13, total 1.38).

So VAT is still computed once on the subtotal. A quick way to settle it with finance: look up an invoice with three lines of 1 x 0.25 at 10% in Ledgerline. VAT on the subtotal gives 0.08 (total 0.83); per-line VAT gives 0.09 (total 0.84). If Ledgerline shows 0.84, or one-cent differences remain on multi-line invoices after this fix, change `invoice_totals` to sum `_round_cent(line_net(qty, price) * rate)` over the lines.

Also unchecked: half-up here means ties round away from zero (-0.125 becomes -0.13). I do not know how Ledgerline treats credit notes.
